source: A general-purpose values vocabulary for the Values vs. Spending Audit, with a DEFAULT mapping onto the categories in data/expense_categories.json. The vocabulary is deliberately small and plain; it is not drawn from any particular psychological instrument and does not claim to be one.
note: SPEC.md Section 13, Tier 2. The default mapping below is a starting point, not a claim — whether groceries serve Health or Home is a question about a person's life, not a fact, so the room lets them reassign every category and stores their answer. Each category appears under AT MOST ONE value: shares have to add up, and a category counted under two values would double-count the money. test/run.js asserts that disjointness and that every category in expense_categories.json is either mapped here or deliberately left out.
unassignedLabel: Not claimed by anything you named

values.label: Security & stability
values.blurb: Not lying awake about money. Cover, cushions, and balances going down.

values.label: Home & comfort
values.blurb: A place that feels like yours, and warm.

values.label: Health & how you feel
values.blurb: Eating well, staying well, looking after the body you live in.

values.label: Freedom & future options
values.blurb: Money that buys choices later — including the choice to stop.

values.label: People & connection
values.blurb: Time with the people you like, and giving to the ones you love.

values.label: Experiences & adventure
values.blurb: Going places, seeing things, having stories afterwards.

values.label: Getting around on your own terms
values.blurb: Being able to go where you need to go, when you need to go.

values.label: Caring for family
values.blurb: The people who depend on you, and what that costs.

values.label: Ease & good things
values.blurb: Convenience, nice objects, the small stuff that makes a week easier.

unmappedNote: "Everything else" is deliberately unmapped. Money that lands there has not been claimed by anything, which is itself worth seeing.
